entities.summary:
The COVID-19 pandemic in Spain, a significant regional impact, unfolded from late 2020 to 2022, taking a substantial toll on the country's healthcare system and economy.

The pandemic, caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, spread rapidly across Spain, infecting millions and claiming thousands of lives, with the worst-affected regions being the Madrid metropolitan area and the Valencia region.

The COVID-19 pandemic in Spain had far-reaching consequences, including a significant increase in reported cases, hospitalizations, and deaths, as well as a devastating impact on the country's economy, with widespread lockdowns and closures of businesses.

The pandemic also spurred significant changes in public health policies and practices, with the implementation of strict measures such as mask-wearing, social distancing, and vaccination campaigns, which would have lasting implications for public health in Spain.

In the words of Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, 'This pandemic has been a test of our resilience, our solidarity, and our capacity for collective action.'

The COVID-19 pandemic in Spain serves as a poignant reminder of the devastating impact of global health crises on local communities and economies, highlighting the need for robust public health infrastructure and coordinated international responses to mitigate the effects of such pandemics.
